blocks.text: 1. Executive Summary

Between July and November 2026, AI (Claude Code) was used as a daily working tool in SAP ABAP delivery on three projects running in parallel: PAL, ONGC Videsh (OVL) and Astral through KPMG. It supported the full development cycle: reading functional specifications and legacy code, building new objects, correcting existing ones, ATC remediation, root-cause analysis of dumps and production issues, and technical documentation.

74 developments were completed with AI assistance, covering 312 custom SAP objects built, changed or analysed. They include complete applications (CDS / RAP dashboards, an approval workflow, a forecasting application), reports, interfaces, enhancements, forms and developer tools. Every object was reviewed, activated and tested by the consultant before release.
Conventional delivery of the same scope would take about 1,157 hours. With AI it took 699 hours of working time: **458 hours (57 man-days) saved, a 40% effort reduction.**

blocks.text: 3. How AI Was Used in Daily Delivery
The same five-step loop ran on every project:

items: **Intake** - the issue mail, functional specification or change request is triaged into a work queue.
**Fresh source** - the current version is downloaded from SAP and compared with the last copy, so that nobody else's change is lost.
**AI build or diagnosis** - Claude Code reads the source, dump or trace and writes the new or corrected object, with change markers and the old code kept commented.
**Activation and test** - the consultant pastes or imports the object, activates it, feeds activation errors back and tests with the functional consultant.
**Record** - issue, cause and fix are logged per object and committed, so that every change is traceable.

blocks.text: 4. PAL Project - Detailed AI Use Cases
Philippine Airlines (systems DS4, QS4, PS4): finance and purchasing corrections raised as incidents (INC01192, INC01740, INC01967) and one new approval workflow.
Key developments
**FB70 customer credit memo approval on the GL journal workflow with stage e-mails** (UC-001)

items: **Requirement.** A customer credit memo parked in FB70 must be approved by one to three sequential approvers by amount, then posted automatically. Rejected documents are corrected and resubmitted, with e-mails at each stage.

**AI contribution.** Designed and built the trigger function modules, class ZCL_CM_WORKFLOW with four mail body builders, an RFC mail wrapper and six implicit enhancements (12 source files, 2,146 lines). Diagnosed each G/L-only check and fixed the resubmit by rewriting AWTYP to BKPFF.

**Result.** Approval routing and posting work end to end in DEV client 400 (27/10/26). Standard-code changes are guarded enhancements for document type DG, switchable in SE19. Parked and posted mails confirmed in DEV on 30/10/26.

blocks.text: **PAL Upload General Journal Entry: Excel local and group amounts restored on posting** (UC-002)

items: **Requirement.** When an uploaded journal entry request is rejected, edited and approved, the posted document must carry the local and group currency amounts from the Excel file, not amounts re-derived from exchange rates.

**AI contribution.** Diagnosed the original 48-line method and a mapping error that stored the local amount as the group amount. Delivered a rewritten UPDATE_AMOUNT (889 lines) that matches Excel lines to line items per G/L account, logs to SLG1 and leaves the document untouched without a single fit.

**Result.** Parked documents posted after approval carry the Excel local and group amounts, and every outcome is logged to SLG1. Matching logic checked against brute force on 6,000 random cases with no mismatch. Delivered 14/10/26.

blocks.text: **PAL customer invoice forms: e-mailed PDF could not be opened (INC01967)** (UC-003)

items: **Requirement.** Invoice PDFs e-mailed by the program could not be opened in Acrobat or Edge, while the same document saved manually opened. Customers must receive a readable PDF and the mail log must not report success for a broken mail.

**AI contribution.** Rebuilt one source per include from a 7,084-line print listing and isolated the unchecked write, encrypt and read-back round trip. Delivered the corrected include ZFI_03_CUSTINV_FORM (5,020 to 5,197 lines) and named the narrow authorisation set needed.

**Result.** Every return code in the mail chain is checked, nothing is sent on error and the log shows the reason. Role assignment confirmed on 13/10/26: the mail now carries a readable PDF and the incident symptom is closed.

The JIB Status dashboard is described in section 13.
Key developments
**ZPRA DPR rebuild: Fiori dashboard, CDS/RAP backend and CPI inbound interface** (UC-007)

items: **Requirement.** Rebuild the DPR Excel (actual vs target BOEPD, performance table, summary download) as CDS/RAP services and a Fiori dashboard with six cards. Let CPI post about 20 daily records in one OData call and reconcile interface data with manual entries.

**AI contribution.** Built the Overview Page dashboard with six cards and four detail apps, new views ZDPR_Q_DASH_FILTER and ZDPR_Q_BOEPD_TOTAL and the classic-view rewrite of ZDPR_Q_PROD_PERF. Designed the $batch changeset handling in the OData class, fixed zero-valued measures creating rows and produced three reconciliation workbooks.

**Result.** The dashboard and four detail apps are deployed (TR OCQK901673, 17/09/26) and the cards load in the preview. Zero-valued measures no longer create rows. Reconciliations show the remaining differences come from the CPI mapping.

blocks.text: **Bank Revaluation report for Group Reporting: mapping table and CDS views** (UC-011)

items: **Requirement.** FI / Group Reporting wants the period-end bank revaluation sheet as a Fiori analytical query: per bank G/L account the balance, participating-interest (PI) share, key-date rate to USD and revalued USD balance. The app-built query lacked PI share and rate.

**AI contribution.** Designed the mapping table ZFI_BR_GLMAP, ZBR_PISHARE, the three CDS views, an import ZIP and a 48-row SM30 load sheet. Diagnosed the activation errors, the missing C1 release, the T012K redirect and a join fan-out, and reconciled the client's 18/11 extraction account by account (39 split accounts tie, 0 exceptions).

**Result.** The query shows PI share, rate type, exchange rate, house bank and account number per bank account, with the PI share held in a maintainable table. The views were active on 03/11/26 and the house-bank fan-out was closed on 17/11/26.

blocks.text: **Per Barrel Analysis board agenda: CDS cube and analytical query on ZFI_AGENDA** (UC-010)

items: **Requirement.** Finance prepares the Per Barrel Analysis workbook for the board agenda: per project, oil and gas, price, cost, royalty, transportation, DD&A and profit per barrel by year and period. The ask was a CDS cube in Custom Analytical Queries.

**AI contribution.** Built table function ZI_PBA_AGENDA_TF, AMDP class ZCL_PBA_AGENDA_TF (331 lines), views ZI_PBA_ITEM and ZI_PBA_CUBE and an import ZIP. The cube output (1,322 rows) and two query exports (88 of 88 and 152 of 152 values) equal SAP. Gave the query set-up, calculated-measure formulas and tile URL.
**Result.** The cube and query reproduce the PBA sheet, with query exports tying out to SAP values. The objects were active on 10/11/26 and the quarter change on 12/11/26.

blocks.text: **Asset impairment and write-back posting: batch input replaced by FI-AA BAPIs for S/4** (UC-017)

items: **Requirement.** The impairment and write-back posting (ZFIIMPR, then ZAAIMP) stopped in SM35 after the S/4 conversion with 'LEAVE TO TRANSACTION is not allowed in batch input'. Posting had to work again for all six modes.

**AI contribution.** Diagnosed the dispatcher redirect and mapped mode, screen and transaction for the seven call sites. Delivered MZAAIMPF01 (237 to 658 lines, new BAPI FORMs) and MZAAIMPI01 (1,436 to 1,925 lines) with check-then-post per row and a per-asset run log, the old code commented in place.
**Result.** Both includes were activated on 27/08/26 and verified against a closed fiscal year: every asset returns a readable message from the BAPI check instead of a buried batch-input log.

blocks.text: **ZFI_ACDOCA_JVA_ALIGN: Excel upload posting JVA alignment lines to ACDOCA ledger 0L** (UC-015)

items: **Requirement.** Ledger 0L lacks the venture / equity group / recovery indicator split of the JV ledger, and Group Reporting reads 0L. The split is inserted from an Excel file as ACDOCA-only lines, with a default test run and an undo, without moving any account balance.

**AI contribution.** Built the report (1,793 lines after five iterations), a TS, a 15-item assumptions sheet and a Python builder that checks 172 recon rows net to zero per account (40 accounts). Resolved 15 syntax errors, reworked the recovery-indicator rule, added an OLE fallback reader and added posting key, BTTYPE and CBTTYPE.

**Result.** The report defaults to a test run, posts balanced documents per company code, year and period, and offers an undo with authority checks. A one-account file posted as ZJVA000001 and the reconciliation showed zero on 03/11/26.

blocks.text: 8. ATC Correction and Code Optimisation Summary

The ATC S/4HANA-readiness findings assigned for ONGC were worked family by family, so that each correction pattern was derived once and reused across the batch: about 88 hours conventionally against 64 hours with AI, including review and correction.

blocks.caption: Main finding types and the correction applied
rows: SELECT SINGLE without a unique key
Full key supplied where available; otherwise SELECT with ORDER BY on the key fields and UP TO 1 ROWS, so the result is deterministic.
BINARY SEARCH or DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES on unsorted data
SORT on exactly the compared fields, placed before the statement and outside any loop.
Variables retyped to the data element or converted explicitly; pseudo-comment with the SAP note only where no truncation can occur.
Read through the released CDS view I_OperationalAcctgDocItem with field aliases; cluster-specific constructs removed.
Read through the compatibility view V_KONV in strict Open SQL; CLIENT SPECIFIED and the client field dropped together.
Simplified object: VBUK / VBUP status tables
Status fields read from VBAK / VBAP / LIKP / LIPS or the compatibility views V_VBUK_S4 / V_VBUP_S4.
Reads moved to LFA1 / KNA1 according to SAP note 2877717, with the type references updated.
CLIENT SPECIFIED and the client condition removed; kept only on real transparent tables.
Open SQL not in strict mode
Comma-separated field lists, host variables escaped with @, clause order corrected.
FOR ALL ENTRIES without a guard
IS NOT INITIAL check on the driver table before every FOR ALL ENTRIES.
Batch input on transactions changed in S/4HANA
Replaced by released BAPIs, with the return messages mapped back to the caller.
Rewritten in Open SQL where practical; non-HANA hints removed.

blocks.text: Examples of AI-assisted correction logic
Generic patterns as applied across the batch (illustrative statements, not client code).

blocks.caption: Example 1 - SELECT SINGLE without a unique key
lines: * Before
SELECT SINGLE belnr FROM bkpf INTO lv_belnr WHERE bukrs = p_bukrs AND xblnr = lv_ref.
* After - deterministic result, strict Open SQL
SELECT belnr FROM bkpf WHERE bukrs = @p_bukrs AND xblnr = @lv_ref
ORDER BY belnr INTO @lv_belnr UP TO 1 ROWS.
ENDSELECT.

blocks.caption: Example 2 - simplified object: KONV pricing read moved to the compatibility view
lines: * Before
SELECT kschl kbetr FROM konv CLIENT SPECIFIED INTO TABLE lt_cond
WHERE mandt = sy-mandt AND knumv = lv_knumv.
* After - CLIENT SPECIFIED and the client field dropped together
SELECT kschl, kbetr FROM v_konv WHERE knumv = @lv_knumv INTO TABLE @lt_cond.

blocks.caption: Example 3 - FOR ALL ENTRIES guarded, driver de-duplicated on the full key
lines: SORT lt_docs BY bukrs belnr gjahr.
DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM lt_docs COMPARING bukrs belnr gjahr.
IF lt_docs IS NOT INITIAL.
SELECT bukrs, belnr, gjahr, buzei, hkont FROM bseg FOR ALL ENTRIES IN @lt_docs
WHERE bukrs = @lt_docs-bukrs AND belnr = @lt_docs-belnr AND gjahr = @lt_docs-gjahr
INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_items).
ENDIF.

blocks.caption: Documented correction patterns (72)
rows: NOORDER - SELECT SINGLE on a partial key
Convert to SELECT <fields> FROM <t> WHERE <cond> ORDER BY PRIMARY KEY INTO @tgt UP TO 1 ROWS, closed by ENDSELECT, without SINGLE; on a projection ORDER BY the selected key fields.
NOORDER - cluster/pool table or cursor without ORDER BY
Add ORDER BY PRIMARY KEY (SELECT *) or ORDER BY the selected key fields; keep CDPOS/CDHDR cursor paging and only add ORDER BY PRIMARY KEY.
Replace with SELECT SINGLE @abap_true FROM t WHERE <cond> INTO @DATA(lv_exists), keep the sy-subrc logic and remove the leftover loop.
NOORDER - READ TABLE BINARY SEARCH without SORT
Insert SORT itab BY <WITH KEY fields> before the enclosing LOOP; do not duplicate an identical existing SORT.
NOORDER - DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES, AT NEW, ON CHANGE OF
SORT before the loop on exactly the compared fields (plain SORT if none), placed outside any loop.
NOORDER - first-row access (READ INDEX 1, LOOP with EXIT)
Add the inline pseudo-comment #EC CI_NOORDER to the statement.
NOORDER - WRITE/EXIT/RETURN inside a SELECT loop
The finding is reported inside the loop body: add ORDER BY to the enclosing SELECT, or set #EC CI_NOORDER on the reported line; do not append ORDER BY there.
NOORDER on a FOR ALL ENTRIES SELECT
ORDER BY is not allowed with FOR ALL ENTRIES; use the #EC CI_NOORDER pseudo-comment instead.
SORT the internal table before handing it to the ALV factory.
Field Length Extension - type and length conflict messages
Use CONV #( ) to the MATNR or amount type, or retype the variable to the field's data element, then add #EC CI_FLDEXT_OK[note] as the resolution marker.
Field Length Extension - generic parameter messages
Add ACCEPTING PADDING to the IMPORT statement.
Rework the offset access; if no clean fix exists, use #EC CI_FLDEXT_OK[2215424].
Field Length Extension - RFC function parameter type
Interface parameters in generated includes are normally false positives; review the interface in SE37 before changing anything.
Pass MATERIAL_LONG or CONV #( ) only where a narrower value goes into the BAPI structure; otherwise #EC CI_USAGE_OK or CI_FLDEXT_OK[note]. The BAPI is not replaced.
Use CL_MATNR_CHK_MAPPER=>CONVERT_ON_OUTPUT/INPUT, cl_cls_chk_mapper=>convert_char_value_on_output/input, or CONV DMBTR( ) for explicit conversion.
Use CONV #( ) where an amount goes to a non-extended target; otherwise #EC CI_FLDEXT_OK[2610650].
Review each usage; fix only where code truncates the material number to 18 characters, otherwise #EC CI_FLDEXT_OK[2215424].

blocks.text: Annex C - Effort Calculation and Assumptions
A. Effort without AI

Conventional effort per use case = baseline hours for its work type and complexity x scope factor (above 1 where one delivery contains several objects). The baseline covers requirement understanding, analysis, design, coding, debugging, unit testing and documentation. The ATC baseline uses the correction blocks applied: 10 / 25 / 40 minutes per pseudo-comment / replacement / new-code block, 15 minutes per include and 8 hours of packaging.

blocks.caption: Baseline by work type and complexity (hours)

blocks.text: B. Actual effort with AI

All working time of the period is counted: 69 days from 19/08/26 (63 weekdays after leave and 6 weekend days) x 8 hours = 552 hours, plus the dated work from 20/07/26. The hours are distributed over the use cases by their size (70%) and by the measured AI session time of each object (30%), with a minimum per use case for prompting, review, activation and unit testing (1 / 2 / 4 / 8 hours by complexity; 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 3 hours for analyses). Review and correction time is therefore included in every figure.
C. Calculation

items: Effort saved (hours) = effort without AI - actual effort with AI.
Effort reduction (%) = effort saved / effort without AI x 100.
Effort saved (man-days) = effort saved in hours / 8.
Productivity improvement (%) = (effort without AI / actual effort with AI - 1) x 100.
Project totals are weighted by hours, not averaged percentages. Recurring savings from automation are separate from these development savings.
